scope: Isolated Castle Game Engine WebGL matrix and numeric-list conversion candidate: contiguous-layout checks, signed-byte bounds, owned bulk copies, reproducible baseline/candidate Pascal transfer tests and correctly bound candidate application staging. Application dependency adoption and existing buffer-upload helpers are outside this development-candidate scope.

intuitiveness.evidence: The retained harness exposes explicit baseline and candidate commands, a required signed-range switch, useful failure diagnostics and source/WASM metadata. The final application comparison also records the exact fixture, run order and hash-bound sites.

accuracy.evidence: The candidate wrapper passes 9506 checks: 9493 legacy plus 13 signed-boundary checks, with no browser errors. Verification binds the candidate engine source SHA-256 c4da0f1642a8ae3470f802a93ee647a362907d9fa18e82f0a209453e8984d081 to probe WASM a90a5d98a77aeb5cf5e2cfb5ad846dcc1ed4ba313eefadad2e0d95e0e7e8fa95. The updated pinned baseline passes all 9493 legacy checks with the candidate guard explicitly skipped. The size-12 paired application fixture has identical draw counts per frame, exact world recovery, zero renderer errors and zero differing pixels in desktop, phone-layout and recovered captures.

wowFactor.evidence: The candidate delivers a measured roughly 50 percent frame-rate increase on the paired development fixture: 9.84 to 14.74 fps desktop Orbit, 10.08 to 15.56 phone-layout Orbit, 25.55 to 38.81 phone walking and 25.72 to 38.93 after recovery. The comparison reports byte-identical and pixel-identical screenshots for all three pairs.

thinkingOutOfTheBox.evidence: The design combines compile-time layout contracts, owned raw copies, signed-byte overflow rejection, synthetic logical counts that avoid a 2 GiB allocation, and paired application hashes while preserving the public API and dependency pin.
